title: John Rush: Go deep on one project, price at $49+, use AI SEO, and don't quit your job
summary: John Rush argues indie hackers should go deep on one project instead of launching many MVPs, and learn every founder skill over time. He covers lessons from buying an $800k product (Unicorn Platform), pricing so customers actually need the product, SEO as both traffic and copy, and not quitting your job.

principles.text: Don't spray MVPs hoping one sticks. Add a new founder skill with each project so your odds rise.
principles.quote: you have to increase your skill set over time. So in the first years you learn to build MVPs in the second year you learn to do SEO in the third year you learn to do cold sales in the fourth year you learn UX

principles.text: Go deep on one project. Once it's built, you're forced into marketing, content, SEO and sales.
principles.quote: if the project has been built, and there's no more code to write, then you have no choice but do marketing, content creation, SEO, sales, etc.

principles.text: Customers buy solved problems, not features. A $49 price filters for people who actually need the product.
principles.quote: if people don't pay you 49, it's not because it's too expensive, it's because you they don't need it. And if you make it cheaper, they make pay for it, but they still don't need it.

principles.text: A weak product can't be rescued by marketing. If it isn't doing well, the product is the problem.
principles.quote: If if my product is not doing well, it's because the product is bad, not because the marketing is bad.

principles.text: SEO gives traffic and also better copy, because search terms match how people describe the problem. Start with AI content, then edit it by hand.
principles.quote: the best thing you can do is AI plus human. So, whenever you use a tool that does things for you, go help that tool to do the work better.

principles.text: Don't quit your job early. Less time forces you to focus on what matters.
principles.quote: If you can't build your product with a mild traction by spending just two days a week on the product, even spending 5 days a week will not help you.
